investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (the resource quota for peer-pod VMs is exhausted or the allocatable count is zero), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained unscheduled for 132–155 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out, producing empty evidence objects and a full contract-gap for orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, and remoteState. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes — all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods.

[Likely] The 4 remaining nodes lack the required node label or taint toleration that the remote agent pod's nodeAffinity/nodeSelector demands, permanently excluding them from scheduling regardless of resource availability.

[Possible] A recent scale-down or node failure reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes from a higher count to 2, shrinking the schedulable pool below the demand level at the time of the eval run.
[Possible] The kata.peerpods.io/vm resource limit per node is configured too low relative to concurrent remote agent demand, causing exhaustion under normal load.

[Lower likelihood] A misconfiguration in the pod spec's nodeAffinity or nodeSelector (e.g., a label key/value that no longer matches any node) could have reduced the eligible node pool to only the 2 kata-capable nodes, compounding the capacity problem.

investigation.title: Remote Agents eval failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion prevents pod scheduling across all three remote-agent checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-15 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the 6-node cluster has only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, both of which reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never completed, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) unpopulated and triggering a contract validation failure. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod because the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource was exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes and the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. The pod remained Unschedulable for 148 seconds (remote-agent-state), exceeding the eval's implicit readiness window, causing createAgent to fail before any evidence could be collected. The same condition independently triggered failures in remote-agent-create (132 s) and remote-agent-runtime (142 s), confirming the scheduling bottleneck is the shared upstream dependency for all three checks.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: concurrent eval runs, other workloads, or leaked/stuck VMs from prior runs consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new pods. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in all three sibling check failures.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a label or taint that only 2 nodes carry (the kata peer-pods nodes), so even if VM slots were freed, only those 2 nodes are eligible. If both are unavailable for any reason the cluster has zero scheduling headroom.

Tertiary — VM resource leak from a prior eval run: the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs is responsible for releasing resources; if a previous run's cleanup did not complete (e.g., due to a timeout or crash), VM slots may remain allocated, reducing available capacity for subsequent runs.
Lower confidence — transient cluster scaling lag: the cluster may not have auto-scaled to add a new kata-capable node before the eval's scheduling timeout elapsed.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (the resource quota for peer-pod VMs is exhausted or the allocatable count is zero), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained unscheduled for 132–155 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out, producing empty evidence objects and a full contract-gap for orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, and remoteState. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes — all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods.

[Likely] The 4 remaining nodes lack the required node label or taint toleration that the remote agent pod's nodeAffinity/nodeSelector demands, permanently excluding them from scheduling regardless of resource availability.

[Possible] A recent scale-down or node failure reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes from a higher count to 2, shrinking the schedulable pool below the demand level at the time of the eval run.
[Possible] The kata.peerpods.io/vm resource limit per node is configured too low relative to concurrent remote agent demand, causing exhaustion under normal load.

[Lower likelihood] A misconfiguration in the pod spec's nodeAffinity or nodeSelector (e.g., a label key/value that no longer matches any node) could have reduced the eligible node pool to only the 2 kata-capable nodes, compounding the capacity problem.

investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod because the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource was exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes and the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. The pod remained Unschedulable for 148 seconds (remote-agent-state), exceeding the eval's implicit readiness window, causing createAgent to fail before any evidence could be collected. The same condition independently triggered failures in remote-agent-create (132 s) and remote-agent-runtime (142 s), confirming the scheduling bottleneck is the shared upstream dependency for all three checks.

Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in all three sibling check failures.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a label or taint that only 2 nodes carry (the kata peer-pods nodes), so even if VM slots were freed, only those 2 nodes are eligible. If both are unavailable for any reason the cluster has zero scheduling headroom.

Tertiary — VM resource leak from a prior eval run: the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs is responsible for releasing resources; if a previous run's cleanup did not complete (e.g., due to a timeout or crash), VM slots may remain allocated, reducing available capacity for subsequent runs.
Lower confidence — transient cluster scaling lag: the cluster may not have auto-scaled to add a new kata-capable node before the eval's scheduling timeout elapsed.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Prevents Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required peer-pod VM onto any of the 6 available nodes — 2 nodes reported insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. The eval probe never reached the agent creation step, so zero evidence was collected and the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm schedulable resource on the 2 nodes that match the required node affinity/selector. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every pod submitted by the eval runner for remote agent creation was left in an Unschedulable state for 130–155 seconds before the probe timed out. Because the agent pod never started, the runner could not complete createAgent(), and no evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was produced, causing a full contract violation. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents swarm VM pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189: remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required=true; remote-agent-runtime is required=false, confirming the severity classification is correct but all three checks are impacted.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool exhausted on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: the cluster has consumed all allocatable peer-pod VM slots on the only nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving no schedulable capacity for new eval pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a label or taint that only 2 nodes carry; if those 2 nodes are also at VM capacity, the effective schedulable pool is zero regardless of total cluster size.

Tertiary — cluster autoscaler not configured or not triggered for kata.peerpods.io/vm resource type: peer-pod VM capacity may not be a standard Kubernetes resource that triggers node scale-out, leaving the pool statically bounded.

reproductionSteps.label: Run only the remote-agent-runtime eval probe against production-api
reproductionSteps.details: Use the same environment variables as the scheduled observability workflow. Expect the same Unschedulable scheduler message if VM capacity is still exhausted.

reproductionSteps.label: Run all three remote-agents checks together to confirm the shared scheduling failure
reproductionSteps.details: All three sibling checks failed with the same root cause; running them together will confirm whether the failure is consistent across the full feature.

reproductionSteps.label: Inspect current kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable and used capacity on the cluster
reproductionSteps.details: Use kubectl to describe nodes and check the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource field on each node that matches the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector. Confirm whether allocatable minus requested equals zero.

reproductionSteps.label: Inspect the pending remote-agent pod's scheduling events
reproductionSteps.details: Use kubectl to list pods in the namespace used by the eval runner and describe any pods in Pending state to retrieve the full scheduler event log, confirming the Unschedulable reason matches the eval message.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Kubernetes peer-pod VM scheduling pool
affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler message 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' directly identifies the VM resource pool backing remote agent creation as the exhausted resource. All three remote-agents checks failed because pods could not be placed.

affectedAreas.label: remote-agent-create eval check (required=true)
affectedAreas.reason: Registered as required=true at line 183; failed with latencyMs=134566 and the same Unschedulable message, making this the earliest observable failure in the sequence.

affectedAreas.label: remote-agent-state eval check (required=true)
affectedAreas.reason: Registered as required=true at line 184; failed with latencyMs=155188, confirming the VM pool was still exhausted when this check ran.

affectedAreas.label: remote-agent-runtime eval check (required=false)
affectedAreas.reason: Registered as required=false at line 185; failed with latencyMs=150057. Because it depends on a successfully created remote agent, it cannot pass while the VM pool is exhausted.

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner createAgent() call for remote agent type
affectedAreas.reason: Line 1918 calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId), which submits the pod that the scheduler cannot place. This is the earliest code boundary where the failure manifests in the runner.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on the 2 affinity-matching nodes; if at zero, determine what workloads are consuming all VM slots and whether any can be evicted or scaled down to restore capacity.

Determine whether the cluster autoscaler or peer-pod provider supports scale-out for the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource type; if not, evaluate whether the static VM pool size needs to be increased to handle concurrent eval and production workloads.

Review the node affinity/selector configuration for remote-agent pods to confirm that only 2 of 6 nodes are intended to be eligible; if the selector is overly restrictive, expanding the eligible node pool would increase scheduling resilience.

Confirm that the eval runner's cleanup path (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs line 1916) correctly releases any partially allocated VM resources when a pod fails to schedule, to avoid resource leaks that could worsen pool exhaustion.

Once capacity is restored, re-run all three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) to confirm the feature returns to a passing state before closing the investigation.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Check kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used on all nodes
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly confirms whether the VM resource pool is at capacity on the 2 affinity-matching nodes, proving or disproving the primary exhaustion hypothesis.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: List pending remote-agent pods and retrieve scheduler events
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies any pods left in Pending state from the eval run and allows kubectl describe to retrieve the full scheduler event log matching the eval failure message.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run the failed expected-output contract after checking capacity
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the failure is still present; a pass after capacity is restored would confirm the diagnosis. Continued failure would indicate a persistent capacity or configuration problem.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect node affinity/selector on the remote-agent pod spec
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Narrows whether the 4-node affinity mismatch is expected (correct selector, wrong nodes) or a misconfiguration that is artificially shrinking the schedulable pool.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Retrieve the pod spec used by createAgent() for the 'remote' type and compare its nodeSelector and affinity rules against the labels on all 6 cluster nodes to confirm exactly which 2 nodes are eligible and why 4 are excluded.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node on the 2 affinity-matching nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity greater than zero with no pending pods consuming it, the exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a misconfigured node selector or admission webhook would become the primary suspect.

If the remote-agents eval checks pass on an immediate re-run without any infrastructure change, the failure was transient (e.g., a burst of concurrent agent creation by other workloads temporarily exhausted the pool) rather than a sustained capacity ceiling.
If only remote-agent-runtime fails while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state pass on re-run, the failure is isolated to the runtime check and not a shared VM pool exhaustion.

If the pod spec submitted by the eval runner carries a node selector or affinity that does not match any node in the cluster (configuration error rather than capacity error), the scheduler would report 6/6 nodes with affinity mismatch rather than 2 with insufficient VM and 4 with affinity mismatch — the current split of 2+4 supports capacity exhaustion on the affinity-matching nodes specifically.

If no kata.peerpods.io/vm resource is registered on any node (resource never existed), all 6 nodes would report the same reason; the 2+4 split disproves total absence and confirms partial capacity exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that directly queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity across all cluster nodes and warns before the pool reaches zero, providing earlier signal before agent creation attempts fail.

Add a scheduling-latency eval that measures time-to-schedulable for a remote-agent pod and fires a warning when scheduling latency exceeds a threshold (e.g., 30s), catching pool pressure before it causes full Unschedulable failures.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector is above a minimum threshold, catching configuration drift that shrinks the eligible node pool.

Consider a canary eval that attempts remote agent creation with a short timeout (e.g., 30s) on a fixed schedule, so VM pool exhaustion is detected within one eval cycle rather than only when the full 130–155s probe timeout is reached.
